name: Widowmaker Drift

stars.name: Cold Fury
stars.notes: High rotational velocity creates a pronounced equatorial bulge. Debris disk from planetary formation still partially present.

planets.name: Razorwire
planets.notes: Surface covered in jagged crystalline silicate formations caused by extreme thermal cycling. Landing attempts would shred standard landing gear.

planets.name: Heartbreak
planets.notes: Dense iron-nickel composition with a faint, choking atmosphere of nitrogen and sulfur dioxide. Named by the survey team that lost two members to equipment failure here.

planets.name: The Widow
planets.notes: A massive rocky world with crushing gravity at 2.7g. Thin carbon dioxide atmosphere. Deep canyon systems may harbor subsurface ice deposits.

planets.name: Dreadnaught
planets.notes: Banded hydrogen-helium giant with a violent storm system spanning 40,000 km. Its radiation belt is powerful enough to disable unshielded probes.

planets.name: Exile
planets.notes: Frozen methane and nitrogen world at the system's outer edge. Surface temperature averages -221 C. Extreme isolation makes any rescue operation impractical.

anomalies.name: The Shredding Field
anomalies.location: Inner system, 0.2 to 1.8 AU from Cold Fury
anomalies.notes: Dense remnant proto-planetary disk of high-velocity particulate matter. Equivalent to continuous micro-meteorite bombardment. Danger level: high.

anomalies.name: Dreadnaught's Maw
anomalies.notes: Dreadnaught's immense gravity well creates a capture zone that has claimed at least one probe. Objects entering without sufficient delta-v cannot escape. Danger level: extreme.

asteroid_belts.name: Widow's Teeth
asteroid_belts.composition: iron-nickel and silicate, high metallic content
asteroid_belts.notes: Unusually dense belt with frequent collisions generating secondary debris. Contains significant iron and rare-earth deposits but extraction is hazardous.

stations.name: Marker Buoy WD-1
stations.location: System edge, 45 AU from Cold Fury
stations.notes: Automated hazard beacon broadcasting debris disk warnings and Dreadnaught radiation belt data on all standard frequencies.

faction_control.notes: Unclaimed. The Pale Marches Territorial Authority maintains the navigation buoy but asserts no sovereignty.

history: Survey team Theta-7 conducted the first crewed reconnaissance of Widowmaker Drift in 2527. Two technicians died during an EVA on Heartbreak when their pressure suits failed in the sulfur dioxide atmosphere. The planet was named in their memory.

In 2541, the mining consortium Ferrous Deep dispatched a prospecting fleet to Widow's Teeth. The lead vessel suffered catastrophic hull breaches from debris disk particulates during approach. The expedition was abandoned after three ships sustained damage.

A long-range probe was captured by Dreadnaught's gravity well in 2558 and crushed in the giant's atmosphere, prompting the deployment of Marker Buoy WD-1 to warn incoming traffic of the gravitational hazard.
description: Widowmaker Drift earns its name through attrition. The system's A0V star, Cold Fury, presides over five dead worlds surrounded by a gauntlet of navigational hazards. The remnant proto-planetary disk—the Shredding Field—fills the inner system with high-velocity particulates that sandblast any vessel transiting without heavy armor. Beyond that lie five worlds that offer nothing but danger: razor crystal surfaces, choking atmospheres, crushing gravity, lethal radiation belts, and killing cold.

The system's most insidious threat is its apparent ordinariness. At long range, Widowmaker Drift reads as a standard A-class system with a dense asteroid belt and a gas giant—a plausible mining prospect. It is only upon approach that the true danger becomes clear: the debris disk is far denser than standard surveys suggest, the asteroid belt is in active collision cascade, and Dreadnaught's gravity well extends much further than its mass would predict. By the time these hazards are apparent, course correction may be too late.

The rare-earth deposits in Widow's Teeth remain a tantalizing prize for any mining operation willing to accept catastrophic risk. Several consortiums have conducted feasibility studies; all have concluded that current technology cannot extract the resources safely. Widowmaker Drift waits patiently, a trap baited with wealth that no one can reach.
